chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who prayed toward other than the qiblah, then realizes while he is in the salat, before he has finished his salat. He said: If he was facing within what is between the east and the west, then he should turn his face toward the qiblah when he realizes. But if he was facing toward the back of the qiblah, then he should break off, then turn his face toward the qiblah, then begin the salat.

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer toward which one must face in salat
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the east, used here in defining directional range
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the west, used here in defining directional range
key_terms.دُبُرِ الْقِبْلَةِ: the rear or opposite direction of the qiblah
key_terms.فَلْيَقْطَعْ: he should discontinue or break off the prayer
key_terms.مُتَوَجِّهًا: oriented or facing in a particular direction

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they realize during salat that they were facing the wrong qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who discovers during salat that he was praying in the wrong direction. If his orientation was still within the range between east and west, he turns toward the qiblah and continues; but if he was facing opposite the qiblah, he must discontinue and restart the salat facing correctly.
